The principal characteristic group of the molecule is the carboxylic acid, so the parent name is “benzoic acid’’ and its carbon is numbered 1.  
The other five substituents must then be placed so that  

• the carbaldehyde (-CHO) and the cyano (-CN) groups are each meta to the acid and also meta to each other;  
• the hydroxy (-OH) and the dimethyl-amino (-NMe₂) groups are both ortho to the acid;  
• the methoxy (-OMe) group is para to the acid;  
• the methoxy and the hydroxy groups are each ortho to the nitrile.

The only arrangement that fulfils all those relationships is  

1 – CO₂H  
2 – OH  
3 – CN  
4 – OMe  
5 – CHO  
6 – NMe₂

With these locants the correct substituent list (placing substituents in the usual ascending-locant order) is  

2-hydroxy-3-cyano-4-methoxy-5-formyl-6-(dimethylamino)benzoic acid.

This corresponds to option (A).

Answer: A
